$comment: One shared truth table for FIELD-level sensitivity (CONTRACT-2 C7, extended 2026-09-29). A scope's domain can be standard while one of its fields is an identifier: the same EIN was sensitive under Tax record and standard as 'Fein' under Legal entity, so a Legal entity follow-up would have sent it to the model (localhost acceptance run 4, S3). Read by the Python rule (consent-protocol/hushh_mcp/consent/field_sensitivity.py) and meant to be read by the client the same way before it builds sharedInformation. Unknown keys in a standard domain stay standard; an identifier-class key or an identifier-shaped value is sensitive in ANY domain. Keys are matched as whole words after camelCase and separator splitting, lower-cased, with a trailing plural 's' folded on words longer than three letters and the filler words below removed.
$comment_value_patterns: Regexes in the shared subset of Python and JavaScript syntax (no lookbehind, no named groups). A value is identifier-shaped when any pattern is found in it. A 'luhn' pattern counts only when its digits pass the Luhn checksum, so an ordinary long number is not mistaken for a card.
